\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{ازداد} (izdāda)}{ازداد (izdāda)}]{\ar{ازداد} (izdāda) — to become greater; to increase}

\label{lesson:AR-C412-izdada}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to struggle against, then the Arabic for to approve formally.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{ازداد}}
\textbf{\ar{ازداد}} — \emph{izdāda} — \textquotedblleft{}to become greater; to increase\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{ازداد} \ar{عدد} \ar{السكان}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{izdāda ʿadad as-sukkān.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The number of inhabitants grew.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يزداد}, \emph{yazdād}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{ازداد}} (\emph{izdāda}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{z-y-d}, \textquotedblleft{}to increase, to grow more\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form VIII of \emph{zāda}, to increase: to become greater.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{izdāda}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{izdāda}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{izdāda ʿadad as-sukkān.} — The number of inhabitants grew.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to struggle against, then the Arabic for to approve formally, then say \emph{izdāda} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{ازداد} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To become greater; to increase\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تقلص} (taqallaṣa)}{تقلص (taqallaṣa)}]{\ar{تقلص} (taqallaṣa) — to shrink}

\label{lesson:AR-C412-taqallasa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to approve formally, then the Arabic for to become greater.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تقلص}}

\begin{quote}
\ar{تقلص} \ar{عدد} \ar{الطلاب}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{taqallaṣa ʿadad aṭ-ṭullāb.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The number of students shrank.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يتقلص}, \emph{yataqallaṣ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تقلص}} (\emph{taqallaṣa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{q-l-ṣ}, \textquotedblleft{}to contract, to shrink\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form V, to draw itself in: to shrink.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تضاعف} (taḍāʿafa)}{تضاعف (taḍāʿafa)}]{\ar{تضاعف} (taḍāʿafa) — to double}

\label{lesson:AR-C412-tadaafa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to become greater, then the Arabic for to shrink.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تضاعف}}
\textbf{\ar{تضاعف}} — \emph{taḍāʿafa} — \textquotedblleft{}to double\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{تضاعف} \ar{عدد} \ar{الزوار} \ar{في} \ar{الصيف}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{taḍāʿafa ʿadad az-zuwwār fī aṣ-ṣayf.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The number of visitors doubled in summer.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يتضاعف}, \emph{yataḍāʿaf}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تضاعف}} (\emph{taḍāʿafa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ḍ-ʿ-f}, \textquotedblleft{}the like of a thing; to double\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form VI, to be multiplied by itself: to double.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{قلل} (qallala)}{قلل (qallala)}]{\ar{قلل} (qallala) — to reduce}

\label{lesson:AR-C412-qallala}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to shrink, then the Arabic for to double.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{قلل}}
\textbf{\ar{قلل}} — \emph{qallala} — \textquotedblleft{}to reduce\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{قلل} \ar{الطبيب} \ar{كمية} \ar{السكر}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{qallala aṭ-ṭabīb kammiyyat as-sukkar.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The doctor reduced the amount of sugar.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يقلل}, \emph{yuqallil}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{قلل}} (\emph{qallala}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{q-l-l}, \textquotedblleft{}to be few, little\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form II, to make little: to reduce. \ar{قليل} and \ar{أقل} are from the same root.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{qallala}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{qallala}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{qallala aṭ-ṭabīb kammiyyat as-sukkar.} — The doctor reduced the amount of sugar.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to shrink, then the Arabic for to double, then say \emph{qallala} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{نسبة} (nisba)}{نسبة (nisba)}]{\ar{نسبة} (nisba) — a proportion}

\label{lesson:AR-C412-nisba}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to double, then the Arabic for to reduce.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{نسبة}}
\textbf{\ar{نسبة}} — \emph{nisba} — \textquotedblleft{}a proportion\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{نسبة} \ar{النجاح} \ar{عالية} \ar{هذه} \ar{السنة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{nisbat an-najāḥ ʿāliya hādhihi as-sana.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The proportion of passes is high this year.
\end{quote}

\ar{بالنسبة} \ar{إلى}, \emph{bi-n-nisba ilā}, regarding, as for.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{نسبة}} (\emph{nisba}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{n-s-b}, \textquotedblleft{}to trace lineage, to relate\textquotedblright{} (Lane). A \emph{nisba} is a relation, and so a ratio: a proportion, a percentage.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nisba}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nisba}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nisbat an-najāḥ ʿāliya hādhihi as-sana.} — The proportion of passes is high this year.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to double, then the Arabic for to reduce, then say \emph{nisba} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{نسبة} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A proportion\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
